query: Can a trademark protect the name of my Ayurvedic brand?
summary: Yes. In India a trademark can protect the name of your Ayurvedic brand, because a trade mark can cover names that distinguish one person's goods or services. But there are limits. The name must be distinctive and not merely descriptive, deceptive, or confusingly similar to an earlier mark, and registration is not guaranteed. Importantly, a trademark protects only the branding, not any exclusive rights in the chemical formulation, therapeutic effect, extraction technique, or manufacturing process behind your product. Registration protects the mark for the specific goods/services registered, for renewable ten-year terms. [tm_act]

**Trademark protection and its limits**

Established by source: Under Indian law (s.2(1)(zb)), a trade mark can include names capable of distinguishing one person's goods or services, so a brand name is protectable subject matter. (India; ss.2(1)(zb),3-5,9,11,18,25,28) [tm_act] Sections 9 and 11 (India) restrict registration where a mark lacks distinctiveness, is descriptive or deceptive, or conflicts with an earlier mark. (India; ss.2(1)(zb),3-5,9,11,18,25,28) [tm_act] Section 28 (India) protects the mark only for registered goods/services subject to limits, and s.25 gives renewable ten-year terms. (India; ss.2(1)(zb),3-5,9,11,18,25,28) [tm_act] A trademark does not confer exclusive rights in the formulation, therapeutic effect, extraction technique or manufacturing process (India). (India; ss.2(1)(zb),3-5,9,11,18,25,28) [tm_act] Clearance and choosing a distinctive brand are practical steps, but registration is not assured (India).
